messages:
elaine: Escalation from FinConnect. They started seeing confident-but-wrong timelines after we flipped the 2.7 canary to 20% traffic. Customer says multiple answers now assert incorrect launch years and funding rounds.
kevin: Pasting the customer's repro and one example they provided.
kevin: Prompt: "Summarize AcmePay's launch and funding timeline."
kevin: Model (response): "AcmePay launched in Q3 2016 after a Series A in late 2015 led by Sequoia. By 2018 they expanded to Europe." — Customer: "That's false. AcmePay launched 2019 and Series A was 2020, we have public filings."
kevin: They found ~8 responses across different prompts with assertive but wrong dates/partners since the canary change.
elaine: Severity: customer-visible factual regressions, repeated, impacting trust. CS asked for immediate triage and repro guidance.
cs-bot: Automatic triage: tagged as "model-quality/regression"; created ticket INC-1027; assigned to eng-ml oncall.

sophia: Thanks, copying eng-ml. Can you confirm model id + exact variant used in those requests and the request_id(s)? Also need the raw request (prompt + headers) and a minimal repro we can run against canary vs baseline.
kevin: Provided one request_id: req_202403280942_7f3a. Model in customer logs: redwood-model/2.7-canary-int4. Route: fastpath-low-latency.
sophia: Hypothesis list: 1) Canary variant introduced a prompt conditioning change or reduced safety/penalty weights causing overconfident completions; 2) KV-prefix caching returned stale knowledge blobs (rare but possible with rollout); 3) New quantization path (int4) changed generation surface for dates/numbers. We need to repro locally.
omar: If reproducible and customer impact confirmed roll back canary to 0% immediately. Recommend preserve logs and request ids for postmortem. :warning:
kevin: Repro steps customer shared (they ran from their app). Minimal curl we can use:
kevin: ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" \
  -H "Redwood-Model: redwood-model/2.7-canary-int4" \
  -d '{"prompt": "Summarize AcmePay\'s launch and funding timeline.", "max_tokens": 200}'
```
kevin: Customer also included two more prompts that trigger wrong dates consistently.
sophia: I'll reproduce now against both 2.6-stable and 2.7-canary with identical seeds. Please save request_id(s) if you run it in prod. Also attach tokenization and sampling params if available.
elaine: Customer asked for ETA on fix and whether rollback is possible. They reported this is affecting marketing and docs pages.
sophia: If I can reproduce within 30m, we'll flag for rollback. If not, we'll collect more examples and examine sampling constraints and the int4 quant path. Can someone from runtime share the kernel/quant config used for 2.7-int4? @omar
omar: I'll dump the canary node config and KV-cache versions. Pushing logs for req_202403280942_7f3a to INC-1027 now. :white_check_mark:
kevin: Customer appreciates quick attention. They asked for a copiable set of failing prompts and said they can run more tests if we want.
elaine: Good. Marking as P1 for CS impact. Will keep customer updated every 2 hours until resolved. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
cs-bot: INC-1027 updated: priority=P1, linked to playbook "model-quality-regression". Notifying eng-ml oncall.
sophia: Update: reproduced locally. 2.7-canary-int4 returns confident wrong dates for the AcmePay prompt; 2.6-stable returns correct timeline. Attaching diff and sample outputs to INC-1027. Next steps: run ablation to isolate quant vs prompt-conditioning changes and test with KV-cache disabled.
sophia: Temporary mitigation options: roll back canary -> 0% or force-route FinConnect to 2.6-stable. Recommending immediate rollback until root cause found.
omar: Rolling canary back now. Notifying infra and routing. Will confirm once traffic at 0%.
kevin: I'll tell the customer we've rolled them back and will share update from INC-1027 once eng confirms root cause.
elaine: Thanks team. Please paste final postmortem link into the thread when ready and include recommended guardrails to avoid future regressions (prompt-sanity checks + canary QA for factuality). :pray:
